passages.text: After this I saw another angel descending from heaven with great authority, and the earth was illuminated by his glory.
passages.sermon:
John saw another angel.
This angel came down from heaven.
The angel had great authority.
The angel’s glory shone brightly.
The earth was illuminated by the angel’s glory.
passages.original: Μετὰ ταῦτα εἶδον ἄλλον ἄγγελον καταβαίνοντα ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ἔχοντα ἐξουσίαν μεγάλην καὶ ἡ γῆ ἐφωτίσθη ἐκ τῆς δόξης αὐτοῦ

passages.text: And he cried out in a mighty voice: “Fallen, fallen is Babylon the great! She has become a lair for demons and a haunt for every unclean spirit, every unclean bird, and every detestable beast.
passages.sermon:
An angel appeared.
The angel had great authority.
The angel cried out with a loud voice.
He said, “Babylon the great has fallen.
Babylon has fallen.
Babylon is now a home for demons.
Babylon is a prison for every unclean spirit.
Babylon is a prison for every unclean bird.
Babylon is a prison for every unclean and hated beast.”
passages.original: καὶ ἔκραξεν ἐν ἰσχυρᾷ φωνῇ λέγων Ἔπεσεν ἔπεσεν Βαβυλὼν ἡ μεγάλη καὶ ἐγένετο κατοικητήριον δαιμονίων καὶ φυλακὴ παντὸς πνεύματος ἀκαθάρτου καὶ φυλακὴ παντὸς ὀρνέου ἀκαθάρτου καὶ φυλακὴ παντὸς θηρίου ἀκαθάρτου καὶ μεμισημένου

passages.text: All the nations have drunk the wine of the passion of her immorality. The kings of the earth were immoral with her, and the merchants of the earth have grown wealthy from the extravagance of her luxury.”
passages.sermon:
Babylon is a symbol of great evil and immorality.
All the nations have drunk the wine of her passionate immorality.
The kings of the earth acted immorally with her.
The merchants of the earth became rich from her extravagant luxury.
passages.original: ὅτι ἐκ τοῦ οἴνου τοῦ θυμοῦ τῆς πορνείας αὐτῆς πέπωκαν πάντα τὰ ἔθνη καὶ οἱ βασιλεῖς τῆς γῆς μετ’ αὐτῆς ἐπόρνευσαν καὶ οἱ ἔμποροι τῆς γῆς ἐκ τῆς δυνάμεως τοῦ στρήνους αὐτῆς ἐπλούτησαν

passages.text: Then I heard another voice from heaven say: “Come out of her, My people, so that you will not share in her sins or contract any of her plagues.
passages.sermon:
I heard another voice speak from heaven.
This voice spoke to God’s people.
The voice said, “Come out of Babylon.”
God’s people must leave Babylon.
If you stay, you will share in her sins.
If you stay, you will receive her plagues.
passages.original: Καὶ ἤκουσα ἄλλην φωνὴν ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ λέγουσαν Ἐξέλθατε ὁ λαός μου ἐξ αὐτῆς ἵνα μὴ συνκοινωνήσητε ταῖς ἁμαρτίαις αὐτῆς καὶ ἐκ τῶν πληγῶν αὐτῆς ἵνα μὴ λάβητε

passages.text: For her sins are piled up to heaven, and God has remembered her iniquities.
passages.sermon: Her sins reach up to heaven.\r\nGod remembers her wrongdoings.
passages.original: ὅτι ἐκολλήθησαν αὐτῆς αἱ ἁμαρτίαι ἄχρι τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καὶ ἐμνημόνευσεν ὁ Θεὸς τὰ ἀδικήματα αὐτῆς

passages.text: Give back to her as she has done to others; pay her back double for what she has done; mix her a double portion in her own cup.
passages.sermon:
God speaks about a sinful city.
This city has done evil to others.
God commands people to repay her for her actions.
Give back to her what she has done to others.
Pay her back double for her deeds.
Prepare a double portion for her in her own cup.
Let her receive twice as much as she gave.
passages.original: ἀπόδοτε αὐτῇ ὡς καὶ αὐτὴ ἀπέδωκεν καὶ διπλώσατε τὰ διπλᾶ κατὰ τὰ ἔργα αὐτῆς ἐν τῷ ποτηρίῳ ᾧ ἐκέρασεν κεράσατε αὐτῇ διπλοῦν

passages.text: As much as she has glorified herself and lived in luxury, give her the same measure of torment and grief. In her heart she says, ‘I sit as queen; I am not a widow and will never see grief.’
passages.sermon:
Babylon is a great city.
Babylon glorified herself.
Babylon lived in luxury.
Give Babylon as much torment and grief as the glory and luxury she had.
In her heart, Babylon says, “I sit as queen.”
She says, “I am not a widow.”
She says, “I will never see grief.”
passages.original: ὅσα ἐδόξασεν αὑτὴν καὶ ἐστρηνίασεν τοσοῦτον δότε αὐτῇ βασανισμὸν καὶ πένθος ὅτι ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ αὐτῆς λέγει ὅτι Κάθημαι βασίλισσα καὶ χήρα οὐκ εἰμί καὶ πένθος οὐ μὴ ἴδω

passages.text: Therefore her plagues will come in one day— death and grief and famine— and she will be consumed by fire, for mighty is the Lord God who judges her.”
passages.sermon:
Babylon is a great and powerful city.
Babylon has glorified herself and lived in luxury.
Babylon has said in her heart, “I sit as queen. I am not a widow. I will never see grief.”
Because of this, her plagues will come in one day.
Death will come to her.
Grief will come to her.
Famine will come to her.
Fire will consume her.
The Lord God is mighty.
The Lord God judges her.
passages.original: διὰ τοῦτο ἐν μιᾷ ἡμέρᾳ ἥξουσιν αἱ πληγαὶ αὐτῆς θάνατος καὶ πένθος καὶ λιμός καὶ ἐν πυρὶ κατακαυθήσεται ὅτι ἰσχυρὸς Κύριος ὁ Θεὸς ὁ κρίνας αὐτήν

passages.text: Then the kings of the earth who committed sexual immorality and lived in luxury with her will weep and wail at the sight of the smoke rising from the fire that consumes her.
passages.sermon:
The kings of the earth will see her destruction.
These kings committed sexual immorality with her.
They also lived in luxury with her.
They will weep for her.
They will wail for her.
They will see the smoke from the fire that destroys her.
passages.original: Καὶ κλαύσουσιν καὶ κόψονται ἐπ’ αὐτὴν οἱ βασιλεῖς τῆς γῆς οἱ μετ’ αὐτῆς πορνεύσαντες καὶ στρηνιάσαντες ὅταν βλέπωσιν τὸν καπνὸν τῆς πυρώσεως αὐτῆς

passages.text: In fear of her torment, they will stand at a distance and cry out: “Woe, woe to the great city, the mighty city of Babylon! For in a single hour your judgment has come.”
passages.sermon:
Babylon is a great city.
Babylon is a mighty city.
God judges Babylon.
God is mighty.
God brings judgment quickly.
The kings of the earth see Babylon’s torment.
They fear her suffering.
They stand far away.
They cry out in fear.
They say, “Woe, woe to the great city!”
They say, “Woe to the mighty city of Babylon!”
They say, “Your judgment has come in a single hour.”
passages.original: ἀπὸ μακρόθεν ἑστηκότες διὰ τὸν φόβον τοῦ βασανισμοῦ αὐτῆς λέγοντες Οὐαὶ οὐαί ἡ πόλις ἡ μεγάλη Βαβυλὼν ἡ πόλις ἡ ἰσχυρά ὅτι μιᾷ ὥρᾳ ἦλθεν ἡ κρίσις σου

passages.text: And the merchants of the earth will weep and mourn over her, because there is no one left to buy their cargo— cargo of gold, silver, precious stones, and pearls; of fine linen, purple, silk, and scarlet; of all kinds of citron wood and every article of ivory, precious wood, bronze, iron, and marble; of cinnamon, spice, incense, myrrh, and frankincense; of wine, olive oil, fine flour, and wheat; of cattle, sheep, horses, and chariots; of slaves and souls of men.
passages.sermon:
The merchants of the earth will weep over her.
They will mourn for her.
No one buys their cargo anymore.
Their cargo includes gold.
It includes silver.
It includes precious stones.
It includes pearls.
It includes fine linen.
It includes purple cloth.
It includes silk.
It includes scarlet cloth.
It includes all kinds of citron wood.
It includes every article of ivory.
It includes every article made from precious wood.
It includes bronze.
It includes iron.
It includes marble.
It includes cinnamon.
It includes spice.
It includes incense.
It includes myrrh.
It includes frankincense.
It includes wine.
It includes olive oil.
It includes fine flour.
It includes wheat.
It includes cattle.
It includes sheep.
It includes horses.
It includes chariots.
It includes slaves.
It includes the souls of men.
passages.original: Καὶ οἱ ἔμποροι τῆς γῆς κλαίουσιν καὶ πενθοῦσιν ἐπ’ αὐτήν ὅτι τὸν γόμον αὐτῶν οὐδεὶς ἀγοράζει οὐκέτι γόμον χρυσοῦ καὶ ἀργύρου καὶ λίθου τιμίου καὶ μαργαριτῶν καὶ βυσσίνου καὶ πορφύρας καὶ σιρικοῦ καὶ κοκκίνου καὶ πᾶν ξύλον θύϊνον καὶ πᾶν σκεῦος ἐλεφάντινον καὶ πᾶν σκεῦος ἐκ ξύλου τιμιωτάτου καὶ χαλκοῦ καὶ σιδήρου καὶ μαρμάρου καὶ κιννάμωμον καὶ ἄμωμον καὶ θυμιάματα καὶ μύρον καὶ λίβανον καὶ οἶνον καὶ ἔλαιον καὶ σεμίδαλιν καὶ σῖτον καὶ κτήνη καὶ πρόβατα καὶ ἵππων καὶ ῥεδῶν καὶ σωμάτων καὶ ψυχὰς ἀνθρώπων

passages.text: And they will say: “The fruit of your soul’s desire has departed from you; all your luxury and splendor have vanished, never to be seen again.”
passages.sermon:
Babylon was a great and powerful city.
People desired many things in Babylon.
They will say to Babylon, “The fruit you longed for is gone from you.”
All your luxury has disappeared.
All your splendor has vanished.
No one will ever find these things again.
passages.original: Καὶ ἡ ὀπώρα σου τῆς ἐπιθυμίας τῆς ψυχῆς ἀπῆλθεν ἀπὸ σοῦ καὶ πάντα τὰ λιπαρὰ καὶ τὰ λαμπρὰ ἀπώλετο ἀπὸ σοῦ καὶ οὐκέτι οὐ μὴ αὐτὰ εὑρήσουσιν

passages.text: The merchants who sold these things and grew their wealth from her will stand at a distance, in fear of her torment. They will weep and mourn, saying: “Woe, woe to the great city, clothed in fine linen and purple and scarlet, adorned with gold and precious stones and pearls!
passages.sermon:
The merchants sold these things.
They became rich because of the great city.
They will stand far away.
They will be afraid of her torment.
They will weep.
They will mourn.
They will say, “Woe, woe to the great city!”
This city was clothed in fine linen.
She wore purple and scarlet.
She was adorned with gold.
She had precious stones and pearls.
passages.original: Οἱ ἔμποροι τούτων οἱ πλουτήσαντες ἀπ’ αὐτῆς ἀπὸ μακρόθεν στήσονται διὰ τὸν φόβον τοῦ βασανισμοῦ αὐτῆς κλαίοντες καὶ πενθοῦντες λέγοντες Οὐαὶ οὐαί ἡ πόλις ἡ μεγάλη ἡ περιβεβλημένη βύσσινον καὶ πορφυροῦν καὶ κόκκινον καὶ κεχρυσωμένη ἐν χρυσίῳ καὶ λίθῳ τιμίῳ καὶ μαργαρίτῃ

passages.text: For in a single hour such fabulous wealth has been destroyed!” Every shipmaster, passenger, and sailor, and all who make their living from the sea, will stand at a distance and cry out at the sight of the smoke rising from the fire that consumes her. “What city was ever like this great city?” they will exclaim.
passages.sermon:
God destroyed the great city's wealth in a single hour.
Every shipmaster saw this happen.
Every passenger saw it too.
All sailors saw it.
Everyone who works on the sea saw it.
They all stood far away.
They saw smoke rise from the city's fire.
They cried out when they saw it.
They said, "What city was ever like this great city?"
passages.original: ὅτι μιᾷ ὥρᾳ ἠρημώθη ὁ τοσοῦτος πλοῦτος Καὶ πᾶς κυβερνήτης καὶ πᾶς ὁ ἐπὶ τόπον πλέων καὶ ναῦται καὶ ὅσοι τὴν θάλασσαν ἐργάζονται ἀπὸ μακρόθεν ἔστησαν καὶ ἔκραζον βλέποντες τὸν καπνὸν τῆς πυρώσεως αὐτῆς λέγοντες Τίς ὁμοία τῇ πόλει τῇ μεγάλῃ

passages.text: Then they will throw dust on their heads as they weep and mourn and cry out: “Woe, woe to the great city, where all who had ships on the sea were enriched by her wealth! For in a single hour she has been destroyed.”
passages.sermon:
The people see the great city destroyed.
They throw dust on their heads.
They weep.
They mourn.
They cry out loudly.
They say, “Woe, woe to the great city!”
This city made all who owned ships on the sea rich.
Her wealth brought them great profit.
But in a single hour, the city was destroyed.
passages.original: Καὶ ἔβαλον χοῦν ἐπὶ τὰς κεφαλὰς αὐτῶν καὶ ἔκραζον κλαίοντες καὶ πενθοῦντες λέγοντες Οὐαὶ οὐαί ἡ πόλις ἡ μεγάλη ἐν ᾗ ἐπλούτησαν πάντες οἱ ἔχοντες τὰ πλοῖα ἐν τῇ θαλάσσῃ ἐκ τῆς τιμιότητος αὐτῆς ὅτι μιᾷ ὥρᾳ ἠρημώθη

passages.text: Rejoice over her, O heaven, O saints and apostles and prophets, because God has pronounced for you His judgment against her.
passages.sermon:
Heaven, rejoice over the great city.
Saints, rejoice over the great city.
Apostles, rejoice over the great city.
Prophets, rejoice over the great city.
God has judged the great city.
God has given you justice against her.
passages.original: Εὐφραίνου ἐπ’ αὐτῇ οὐρανέ καὶ οἱ ἅγιοι καὶ οἱ ἀπόστολοι καὶ οἱ προφῆται ὅτι ἔκρινεν ὁ Θεὸς τὸ κρίμα ὑμῶν ἐξ αὐτῆς

passages.text: Then a mighty angel picked up a stone the size of a great millstone and cast it into the sea, saying: “With such violence the great city of Babylon will be cast down, never to be seen again.
passages.sermon:
A mighty angel appeared.
This angel was very strong.
The angel picked up a large stone.
The stone was as big as a great millstone.
The angel threw the stone into the sea.
The angel spoke as he did this.
He said, “With this kind of force, Babylon, the great city, will be thrown down.
No one will ever find her again.”
passages.original: Καὶ ἦρεν εἷς ἄγγελος ἰσχυρὸς λίθον ὡς μύλινον μέγαν καὶ ἔβαλεν εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν λέγων Οὕτως ὁρμήματι βληθήσεται Βαβυλὼν ἡ μεγάλη πόλις καὶ οὐ μὴ εὑρεθῇ ἔτι

passages.text: And the sound of harpists and musicians, of flute players and trumpeters, will never ring out in you again. Nor will any craftsmen of any trade be found in you again, nor the sound of a millstone be heard in you again.
passages.sermon:
Babylon is the great city.
God has judged Babylon.
No one will hear music in Babylon again.
No harpists will play in Babylon again.
No musicians will play in Babylon again.
No flute players will play in Babylon again.
No trumpeters will play in Babylon again.
No craftsmen will be found in Babylon again.
No one of any trade will work in Babylon again.
No one will hear the sound of a millstone in Babylon again.
passages.original: καὶ φωνὴ κιθαρῳδῶν καὶ μουσικῶν καὶ αὐλητῶν καὶ σαλπιστῶν οὐ μὴ ἀκουσθῇ ἐν σοὶ ἔτι καὶ πᾶς τεχνίτης πάσης τέχνης οὐ μὴ εὑρεθῇ ἐν σοὶ ἔτι καὶ φωνὴ μύλου οὐ μὴ ἀκουσθῇ ἐν σοὶ ἔτι

passages.text: The light of a lamp will never shine in you again, and the voices of a bride and bridegroom will never call out in you again. For your merchants were the great ones of the earth, because all the nations were deceived by your sorcery.”
passages.sermon:
Babylon was a great city.
Babylon was powerful and wealthy.
Babylon’s merchants were the most important people on earth.
Babylon deceived all nations by her sorcery.
No lamp will ever shine in Babylon again.
No voice of a bridegroom will be heard in Babylon again.
No voice of a bride will be heard in Babylon again.
passages.original: καὶ φῶς λύχνου οὐ μὴ φάνῃ ἐν σοὶ ἔτι καὶ φωνὴ νυμφίου καὶ νύμφης οὐ μὴ ἀκουσθῇ ἐν σοὶ ἔτι ὅτι οἱ ἔμποροί σου ἦσαν οἱ μεγιστᾶνες τῆς γῆς ὅτι ἐν τῇ φαρμακείᾳ σου ἐπλανήθησαν πάντα τὰ ἔθνη

passages.text: And there was found in her the blood of prophets and saints, and of all who had been slain on the earth.
passages.sermon:
This passage describes a city that God has judged.
God found blood in this city.
The blood belonged to prophets.
The blood belonged to saints.
The blood belonged to all who had been killed on the earth.
God saw that this city was guilty of killing these people.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐν αὐτῇ αἷμα προφητῶν καὶ ἁγίων εὑρέθη καὶ πάντων τῶν ἐσφαγμένων ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς
